object_entity.notes: First ecumenical council convened by Emperor Constantine at Nicaea in Bithynia, May–August 325 CE. Addressed the Arian controversy; produced the original Nicene Creed affirming the Son as homoousios (same substance) with the Father; condemned Arius; standardized Easter dating; addressed the Meletian schism in Egypt. Attended by ~300 bishops, mostly from the East. Jacob of Nisibis and Eusebius of Caesarea were among the attendees.

evidence.notes: Athanasius attended Nicaea as deacon and assistant to Bishop Alexander of Alexandria; he defended homoousios against the Arians.

passage.excerpt: Constantine convened the universal synod at Nicaea in Bithynia, gathering bishops from all regions of the empire.

passage.excerpt: Paraphrase: A philosopher named Meropius of Tyre sailed to India with two boys Frumentius and Aedesius. The ship was seized and all killed except the boys who were brought to the king of Aksum. When the king died the queen asked Frumentius to help govern. Frumentius sought out Roman traders who were Christians and built churches. Later he traveled to Alexandria where Athanasius consecrated him bishop. He returned to Aksum and converted many including the king.
passage.notes: Primary Western source for the christianization of Aksum; Rufinus heard the account from Aedesius himself.
